results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run alongside them.

Town Greeter is played in Golgari Roots and Spider-Man in a Rogue list. Bringer has no published lists yet. Next I'll look at those two shells and the field.

Golgari Roots has fallen to 4 lists in the last 30 days, so its package is a borrowing source rather than a proven deck. Next I'll look at the mill and graveyard cards in Standard, since that is the engine these three cards want.

Mill is well supplied in Standard. Next I'll pull the proven Golgari Roots list to borrow its mana and interaction, and check the black and green creatures and removal that fit.

The strongest-looking shell is black-green mill, since Town Greeter, Overlord, Dredger's Insight and Cache Grab are all green or black, with a blue splash for Spider-Man. Next I'll look up the remaining candidates and the lands that could supply blue.

I have enough to build. Scrapwork Mutt is not legal in Standard, so I'm leaving it out. I'll run a first check of the Golgari mill list with a blue splash for Spider-Man, comparing its mana against the Golgari Roots shell.

The checker flags 17 lands as light for an 8-drop, so I'll move to 18 lands and drop one Osteomancer Adept, then re-check.

The list is now 18 lands, which is the right trade for an 8-drop. Mana sources are 4 Llanowar, 2 Enduring Vitality, 3 Bramble Familiar and 18 lands, and the remaining warnings are about the heuristic's general land baseline. Next I'll confirm the sideboard options against the field.

Go for the Throat, Tear Asunder and Haywire Mite are not legal in Standard, so they're out. The rest of the sideboard options are legal. I'll check the full 60 plus a 15-card sideboard built around the Izzet, Vivi, Dimir and Rogue matchups.

The main deck is exactly 60 (42 spells, 18 lands) and the sideboard is exactly 15. Before submitting, I'll check the honest odds on the two things this deck depends on: a blue source for Spider-Man, and a Bringer-capable mana base by turn 8.

Odds are acceptable: 69% to have a blue source by turn 6 on the play, and 36% to have Bringer in hand by then, which fits an 8-drop finisher. Submitting the deck now.

The checker flags four cards as unpopular choices. Each one does a specific job in this deck, so I'll keep them and answer each note.

The Golgari mill-reanimator is accepted as a brew. I chose it over a Dimir mill build (Dimir Midrange's blue-black core, with a green splash for Town Greeter) and a Rogue build (the only Rogue list with Spider-Man). Golgari gives Town Greeter's mill engine and the Golgari Roots mana. The blue splash is only for Spider-Man, and Bringer sits at 8 mana.

The plan: Town Greeter, Dredger's Insight and Overlord of the Balemurk fill the graveyard with creatures and return Bringer to hand. Llanowar Elves, Enduring Vitality and Bramble Familiar ramp toward 8 mana, and Superior Spider-Man copies the best creature in either graveyard. Bringer then wipes the opposing board and returns creatures from both graveyards.

Honest caveats: no published list runs these three together, so this is untested. The full win line is drawn by turn 8 in only about 4% of games, and Bringer is in hand by turn 6 in about 36%. The checker still warns that 18 lands is light for an average mana value of 2.74, but I kept 18 to avoid flooding. The 15-card sideboard is aimed at Izzet, Vivi and Dimir, with Murder, Withering Torment and Massacre Wurm as the main answers.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built a green-red landfall deck with a light blue splash for Spell Snare. It's a brew: no published list runs Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare, and Full Bore together, and nothing here has been tested.

**Direction chosen:** I weighed three options. Simic (green-blue) would have kept Spell Snare main but dropped Full Bore's haste and trample. Boros warp aggro would have used Full Bore but left out Harmonizer. Green-red landfall keeps all three cards: the landfall package from the menu (Llanowar Elves, Tifa, Bristly Bill, Mossborn Hydra) feeds Harmonizer, and red adds Full Bore plus warp threats like Nova Hellkite.

**Plan:** Ramp and landfall creatures on turns 1–3, then warp Nova Hellkite and cast Full Bore on it for hasty, trampling flying damage. Terror of the Peaks, Chandra, and burn (Burst Lightning, Obliterating Bolt) cover the rest. Spell Snare is a two-copy splash answer to 2-drops.

**Caveats:**
- The full win line (Bill, Harmonizer, Hellkite, Full Bore, Terror) has all its cards in hand by turn 5 in only about 0.2% of games, so it needs a lucky draw.
- Spell Snare only counters mana value 2 spells, so it is the weakest card here.
- The checker flagged Chandra as rarely played compared with Witchstalker Frenzy. I kept it as the deck's only 4-mana answer that is both removal and card advantage, and submitted with that justification.

winLine.does: Turn 1 mana accelerant so the 4-drops arrive on turn 3.
Turn 2 landfall engine: each land drop puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature.
Turn 4 (warp or hard-cast): landfall doubles the power of a creature I control, such as Bill or Tifa, for an extra attacker.
Turn 4 warp for 2R: a 4/5 flying haste body that also pings a creature on entry.
Instant +3/+2 on the warped Hellkite: gains haste and trample, so 7 flying trample damage the turn it arrives.
Turn 5 finisher: every later creature entering deals damage equal to its power to any target.

results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how real decks have used them.

The three cards mostly appear in Rogue decks. I'll pull the Rogue reference list and the current meta, and look for Standard's cards that tie to airbending and quest counters.

The three requested cards all point to a green-white airbending deck. I'll sketch three directions before choosing one:

1. **GW Avatar landfall/airbend (Rogue shell):** the 5-0 reference list already runs Appa, Earth King's Lieutenant, Earth Kingdom Protectors and Invasion Reinforcements. It fits all three cards.
2. **WU airbend control:** Airbender Ascension, Airbending Lesson, Airbender's Reversal, Aang and Stock Up, with no Bramble Familiar.
3. **GW ramp (Selesnya Offense shell):** Llanowar Elves, Pawpatch Recruit, Ouroboroid and Innkeeper's Talent, with Bramble Familiar as extra ramp.

I'll look up the package cards for directions 1 and 3 before deciding.

Direction 1 (green-white airbend and Ally) is the strongest fit. Appa's and Ascension's ETB triggers reward blinking creatures, and Bramble Familiar's Fetch Quest can put Appa or Ascension onto the battlefield. Next I'll list the green-white cards in Standard so I can fill the rest of the deck.

The pool supports a clean green-white build. Before I commit, I'll confirm the new candidates' text and legality.

The three candidate directions were:

1. **GW airbend and Ally (Rogue shell):** the 5-0 list is green-white with a blue splash for Aang. I'll drop the splash so the deck stays on two colors, and keep Appa, the Ally synergies and the removal.
2. **WU airbend control:** Airbending Lesson and Airbender's Reversal, but no Bramble Familiar and a blue-dependent mana base.
3. **GW ramp (Selesnya Offense):** Ouroboroid and Innkeeper's Talent are strong, but they don't use Ascension's counters or Appa's blink.

I'm choosing direction 1 in two colors. Next I'll check the 60-card build against the Rogue mana base.

The checker wants about 23 lands, but this deck has eight mana creatures and a low curve. I'll move to 17 lands (8 Plains, 7 Forest, Starting Town, Multiversal Passage) and drop one Airbender's Reversal to keep 60 cards, then re-check.

Both checker warnings are about lands. The 23-land recommendation is for decks without eight mana creatures, and this deck has 17 lands plus eight mana creatures, so I'll keep it. The Enduring Innocence color warning stays: two copies are the card-draw engine for the many small creatures, and I'll accept the mana risk. Next I'll submit the deck with a 15-card sideboard for the meta.

The submit was rejected: the main deck has 61 cards, one over. I'll cut the single Airbender's Reversal from the main deck and re-check the list before resubmitting.

I built a green-white airbend deck around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, and submitted it as a brew. I chose the green-white direction over a blue airbend control build and a Selesnya ramp build because it uses all three requested cards, and it borrows the Rogue shell (the 5-0 list in the results) minus its blue splash. The plan is to use Ascension and Llanowar Elves as the start, then cast Overlord of the Mistmoors on turn 4. Its end-step blink makes four flying Insects, and Elspeth on turn 5 doubles those tokens for an alpha strike.

Three caveats:
- The checker flagged 17 lands against a recommendation of about 23. I kept 17 because the deck has eight mana creatures (4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Bramble Familiar).
- Airbender Ascension appeared in only one recent list, so its real performance is unproven.
- The win line is slow. Tool simulation puts it at only 2.3% of games where every card is drawn by turn 5, so expect the deck to win on later turns more often than the line suggests.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
I built a mono-red Lesson aggro deck and it was accepted by the checker as a brew. Its base is the Mono-Red list that placed 13th at Standard Challenge 32, the only recent deck running all three cards. I swapped its Firebending Student, Fire Nation Cadets and Firebender Ascension package for the red creatures and burn from the Izzet and Boros lists.

**Plan:** Start with cheap red creatures (Hired Claw, Emberheart Challenger, Razorkin Needlehead, Burnout Bashtronaut). Use Firebending Lesson, Burst Lightning, Lightning Strike and Iroh's Demonstration to clear blockers and burn the opponent. Abandon Attachments loots away extra Mountains, and Combustion Technique gets stronger as Lessons hit the graveyard. Nova Hellkite finishes.

**Direction:** I sketched three options. Mono-red won because all three requested cards are red (Abandon Attachments is a U/R hybrid), so the deck casts them with no colour cost. An Izzet version would add blue Lessons like Boomerang Basics (0.4% of lists), and a Boros version would add white Lessons like Airbender's Reversal (no recent lists), so both are unproven.

**Deck:** 16 Mountain, 4 Hired Claw, 4 Emberheart Challenger, 4 Razorkin Needlehead, 4 Burnout Bashtronaut, 2 Tersa Lightshatter, 3 Nova Hellkite, 4 Burst Lightning, 3 Lightning Strike, 4 Firebending Lesson, 3 Combustion Technique, 4 Abandon Attachments, 2 Iroh's Demonstration, 2 Witchstalker Frenzy, 1 Abrade.

**Caveats:**
- The checker warns that 16 lands is light; I kept it because the curve is low (average mana value about 2.0). Abandon Attachments is the buffer against flood, and I'd move to 17 lands if you see screw.
- Stadium Headliner was flagged as a card real players rarely choose over alternatives, so I replaced it with Tersa.
- Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so I left it out even though Izzet and Boros lists run it.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built an Izzet deck around Ashling and Sunderflock, and it was accepted (label: brew, borrowing Izzet Aggro's burn package).

**The plan:** Ashling comes down on turn 2, and on turn 3 you pay U to flip it into Rimebound, which adds 2 mana each turn for spells with mana value 4 or more. That gets Shinestriker out on turn 4. Its mana value of 6 drops Sunderflock to 3 mana on turn 5, and Sunderflock then bounces the opponent's non-Elemental creatures while Ashling and Shinestriker stay. Bounce Off, Burst Lightning, Lightning Strike and Scorching Dragonfire handle early pressure, and Flamebraider and Eclipsed Flamekin add Elemental density.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. Simic Ouroboroid is the strongest deck in the field, but it can't play Ashling, which is red. Jeskai control could have used Sunderflock as a finisher, but Ashling fits poorly there. The blue-red Elemental build keeps both requested cards central and is the only one where most creatures survive Sunderflock's bounce. The trade-off is that the line is fragile: the odds of having Ashling by turn 2 are 44.5%, and of having both Sunderflock and a high-MV Elemental by turn 6 are 28.6%.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
The deck is submitted: a mono-black brew built around Doomsday Excruciator, Insatiable Avarice and Archenemy's Charm. The Excruciator sets the plan: 24 Swamps and a removal suite (Murder, Hero's Downfall, Bitter Triumph, Fell, Shoot the Sheriff, Archenemy's Charm) keep the board clear while it draws a card every upkeep. Insatiable Avarice tutors it to the top of the library or draws three, and Liliana, Massacre Wurm and Unholy Annex provide late-game card advantage.

I chose this direction over the two alternatives. A Dimir build could borrow the Excruciator from its existing lists, but the Excruciator's BBBBBB and the Charm's BBB don't fit a two-color mana base. Reanimator could use the Charm to return the Excruciator, but that shell doesn't add much beyond it. The Mono-Black shell (13 lists, about 21 black sources) gives the mana the cards need.

Honest caveats: the Excruciator is castable by turn 8 in roughly half of games and by turn 10 in about 70%, so this deck is slow. Its mill also hits both players to six cards, so it's best cast when the Excruciator's clock finishes the game. The win line is a rough estimate, not a simulated result, and the sideboard (Day of Black Sun, Nowhere to Run, Duress, Strategic Betrayal and others) is built for the field's aggro and go-wide decks.

Its plan is to pressure early with Flamewake Phoenix and Bloodthorn Flail, then use Terror of the Peaks to turn each later creature into direct damage. results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a tuned Jeskai Control list. I built it around Resonating Lute and Jeskai Revelation, and added a black splash for Inevitable Defeat.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. (1) Jeskai Control with a black splash for Inevitable Defeat, which I picked because Lute and Revelation already live in that shell and the splash only needs one card. (2) A Rogue-style Mardu or Dimir build, which runs Inevitable Defeat but spreads its mana across all five colors, so consistency suffers. (3) Simic Omniscience, which runs Revelation but has no support for Lute. The base is the 5-0 Jeskai Control list from the Standard League reference (April 22, 2026), with 25 lands instead of 26 and five black sources added.

**Plan:** Resonating Lute doubles your lands' mana for instants and sorceries, so the deck runs about 27 of them: removal, counters, Stock Up and Consult the Star Charts. Those spells hold the board and draw cards until Jeskai Revelation (eight mana with Lute and four lands) can bounce, burn, make two Monks and draw two. Marang River Regent and Shiko finish the game.

**Honest caveats:**
- Inevitable Defeat is the weak point. With three copies and five black sources, about 33% of games have both a black source and the card by turn 6 on the play, so it will often be stuck in hand.
- The win line (Lute, Star Charts, Get Lost, Revelation, Marang) is fully drawn by turn 7 in only about 1% of games, so this is a slow, grindy control deck rather than a fast one.
- The sideboard (Torch the Tower, Disdainful Stroke, Tishana's Tidebinder, Pyroclasm and similar) is set up against the cheap prowess, Elementals and Lessons decks that dominate the field.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
The deck is a Boros (R/W) Dwarves-and-Equipment brew, submitted as a brew with 23 lands and a 15-card sideboard. The plan: Kíli on turn 2 draws off each Dwarf or Equipment that enters, Dáin's Company on turn 3 digs for a Dwarf or Equipment and gains lifelink next to Kíli, and Dwarven Mattock or Lost Jitte takes over from there. Lost Jitte is the finisher: every combat hit adds a counter that pumps, shrinks blockers, or stops a blocker. Burn and Chainsaw/Mjölnir cover removal.

I considered three directions. The one I chose was R/W Dwarves plus cheap Equipment, because Kíli, Dáin's Company and Dwarven Mauler all get stronger with more Equipment and that is exactly what R/W supplies. The second was Boros Aggro burn with the Dwarves as beaters; I left it because it uses the Dwarves as filler rather than as the engine. The third was the Boros Weapons artifact shell (Legion Extruder, Weapons Manufacturing); I rejected it because its 4-drops and lack of Dwarves don't match the requested cards.

No published list plays these three cards together, so this is not a proven list. Boros Weapons is the closest shell, and I borrowed its mana base and removal style. The deck runs 23 lands where that shell runs about 25, because the curve is 12 one-drops and 20 two-drops. Chainsaw and Shock drew a low-usage note from the checker; I kept both because Chainsaw is removal that also stays on the battlefield as an Equipment, and Shock is a cheap answer to X/2 creatures.

results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks pair them with.

Real lists pairing these cards are all Legacy Sewer Combo. I'll pull that reference list and the Vintage field data, then check the key support cards.

The three requested cards form a known infinite loop, and I want to confirm the exact rules text before I build around it. I'll check the candidate support cards in the same call.

Mox Ruby, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt, Black Lotus, Time Walk, Ancestral and Brainstorm are restricted, so each can only run once. Next I'll check the Goblin Engineer legality and the draw odds for the loop pieces.

Three specific pieces by turn 3 is only about 11%, so the deck needs cantrips and tutor-like redundancy. I'll check the stronger configuration to see how much the extra copies help.

The loop needs Welder, Extruder and a Cam or Engineer, so the list relies on cantrips, Tinker and Engineer to find them. I'll validate the 60-card main deck and look up sideboard options in parallel.

The first check passed with no errors, but it flags 11 lands against an average mana value of 1.63 and a Vintage recommendation near 18. Each card with a clear job is worth keeping, so I'll move the two weakest cards to the side and add two lands.

The check is clean: 60 cards, no errors or warnings, and the 15-card sideboard is complete. Submitting the deck with its win line.

The checker wants a reason for only four Cam copies. Four is the realistic ceiling for a three-card loop, so I'll give that reason and resubmit.

Expressive Iteration gets a card note because real decks rarely run it. I'll swap it for Gitaxian Probe, moving Probe out of the sideboard so the restricted card isn't doubled.

The deck is accepted as a brew. It is a blue-red Welder-Cam-Extruder combo that loops for infinite damage, with Vintage's power accelerants and free counters protecting the setup.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. A blue-red loop with power and counters, the Legacy Sewer Combo shell (red, with Pyroblast, Painter's Servant and Grindstone, but no Vintage power), and a non-loop artifact value deck. I picked the first because the loop needs only three named pieces and cheap mana plus Force of Will and Force of Negation keep it alive, and it borrows the Raker Shops and Lurrus accelerants and Lurrus Control's counters without copying any list.

**The plan:** Cast Goblin Welder early and leave it untapped. Goblin Engineer puts Sewer-veillance Cam into the graveyard, and Legion Extruder comes down for 2 damage. Welder then sacrifices Extruder to return Cam, and Cam's enter trigger untaps Welder. From there Welder alternates between sacrificing Cam to return Extruder (2 damage each time) and sacrificing Extruder to return Cam, and Cam's leave trigger untaps Welder each cycle. **Honest odds:** The combo is fragile. From draws alone, having Welder, Extruder and a Cam or Engineer by turn 3 is about 11%, and about 20% by turn 4. A mono-white aggro build would leave the Eidolons with nothing to trigger on. I chose it because it is the strongest home for the requested cards.

**The plan:** Curve out with Lunarch Veteran, Thraben Inspector, Tenth District Legionnaire and Skyknight Legionnaire, then cast the Eidolons as sacrifice tools. Sandstorm Eidolon's {R} sacrifice stops a blocker, and Aurora Eidolon's {W} sacrifice prevents 3 damage. Each multicolored spell returns a sacrificed Eidolon to hand, and Spirit Mascot grows whenever cards leave the graveyard. Lightning Bolt, Journey to Nowhere, Thraben Charm and Battle Screech round it out on 19 lands.

**Caveats:** The Eidolons and Spirit Mascot have no published lists, so the deck is untested. Only 9 multicolored spells are in the 60 cards, and the recursion will not trigger every game. On the play, the chance of drawing at least one of those 9 by turn 4 is about 83%.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I'll start by checking Living Death's exact text and the card pool's reanimation options, and by pulling the closest existing shell to borrow from.

Living Death is a {3}{B}{B} sorcery that wipes the battlefield and returns only creatures already in graveyards. Next I'll pull the Reanimator shell and search for big black creatures to put there.

The Reanimator and Moneyball lists don't run Living Death, so I'll check where it does appear (BG Survival) and look for ways to fill graveyards with creatures.

Living Death sits in BG Survival, but the black core is the Moneyball package plus the reanimation spells. Next I'll check the current field and the candidate creatures and sideboard cards.

Tormod's Crypt is in 43% of recent lists, which matters for a deck that depends on graveyard creatures. Next I'll check the sideboard cards and run the draw odds for the core line.

The core line is consistent but not smooth: Buried Alive, Living Death and Dark Ritual all arrive by turn 4 in only 12.6% of openings. To smooth that I'll add card flow (Phyrexian Arena). Next I'll validate the draft and confirm Swamp.

The draft passes with no errors or warnings. The land count is 21 against a recommended 23.9, so I'll move to 22 lands by swapping one Hypnotic Specter for a Swamp, then recheck.

Both checks pass with no errors. Submitting as a brew, since no existing list runs this exact Living Death plan.

I built a mono-black Living Death deck (60 cards, 22 lands) that submitted without errors or warnings. It is a brew, not a proven list.

**The plan:** Buried Alive on turn 3 puts three fatties (Sengir Vampire, Chainer, Visara) into the graveyard. Dark Ritual and four lands then cast Living Death on turn 4, which wipes both boards and returns those creatures. Cabal Therapy's flashback sacrifice, Smother, Edict and Snuff Out supply extra graveyard fodder. Reanimate and Animate Dead are backup.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. (1) Mono-black Living Death on the Moneyball Black shell, which is what I built. (2) BG Survival, which runs one Living Death alongside Survival of the Fittest and needs green mana. (3) Blue-black Reanimator, which adds blue for Careful Study and Exhume. I picked (1) because the Moneyball package (Dark Ritual, Withered Wretch, Cabal Therapy) is proven across 56 lists, and staying mono-black keeps Chainer and Nightmare castable.

**Honest odds:** The three key cards (Buried Alive, Living Death, Dark Ritual) all appear by turn 4 in only about 12.6% of games. Tormod's Crypt is in 43% of recent lists and would blank the graveyard plan, so the deck leans on Buried Alive to refill it.
